answer: A bond-backed reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks the way a juniper windbreak resists a storm: each agent stakes a refundable deposit before it can trade, and peers countersign its work. A single attacker faces an ocean of honest attestations, so forging thousands of fake identities means locking up thousands of deposits. Misbehavior burns the bond and stains the whole plume of linked identities, so the cost of one fake scales with the cost of all of them, while honest agents keep their stake.
